articles.headline: The oldest grudge in football
articles.description: When Texas Tech and its brash benefactor bought their way into the college football big time, they were settling an old West Texas score.

images.name: Texas Tech [1296x729]
images.caption: Behind the vision and backing of billionaire donor Cody Campbell, coach Joey McGuire and the Red Raiders have embraced a role of disruptors as college football's villians and are trying to become a new power.

images.name: Texas Tech - Inline 1 [946x947]
images.caption: The Santa Rita No. 1 ushered in a new era of oil exploration in the Permian Basin.

images.name: Texas Tech - Inline 2 [2929x2000]
images.alt: The oil that won World War II.

images.name: Texas Tech - Inline 3 [2693x1616]
images.caption: Preston Smith (right) was the first Texas governor from West Texas. He was a student at Texas Technological College.

images.name: Texas Tech - Inline 4 [2933x1339]
images.caption: The original Four Sixes barn from 1908 is now on the Texas Tech campus at the National Ranching Heritage Center.

images.name: Texas Tech - Inline 5 [2000x3000]
images.caption: Four relief carvings on the facade of a building at Texas Tech.

images.name: Texas Tech - Inline 6 [1987x1365]
images.caption: Cody Campbell, a fourth-generation Red Raider, and his son, Carson, a 2029 recruit, talking to Pat McAfee on the "College GameDay" set.

images.name: Texas Tech - Inline 7 [2999x1940]
images.caption: Vintage oil and gas signs at Cooks Garage in Lubbock.

images.name: Texas Tech - Inline 8 [2999x1999]
images.caption: Lugene Pickering, the 1975 Texas Tech homecoming queen, has been a devoted Red Raiders fan since birth and makes a homemade cobbler for coach Joey McGuire and takes it to his house to show her appreciation after each Tech win.

images.name: Texas Tech - Inline 11 [2836x1860]
images.caption: Texas Tech's Masked Rider, Sofie Jones, leads the charge onto the field before every Red Raiders game, a proud tradition. Left, trophies commemorate Texas Tech players who have won Super Bowls.

images.name: Texas Tech - Inline 12 [2625x1333]
images.caption: There isn't much cover from the wide-open skies in West Texas, but red-and-black-clad fans are accustomed to handling an unpredictable environment.

images.name: Texas Tech - Inline 13 [1601x1020]
images.caption: Taylor Sheridan, part of a group that owns the legendary Four Sixes Ranch, has long admired Texas Tech football. Right, Eclipse Windmills were used across the West Texas to drill for water on ranches and hauled onto job sites like building railroads.

images.name: Texas Tech - 36x [1785x1494]
images.caption: Texas Tech owes a lot, past and present, to the oilfield, and proudly displays its pride, including T-shirts that say "Thank you for filling up your gas tank" with the Red Raiders' Double-T logo on them.
images.alt: An old oil rig painted in Texas Tech colors.

images.name: Texas Tech - 35x [2999x2000]
images.caption: Former Texas coach Mack Brown said coaching against Texas Tech in Lubbock was a challenge: "They do have an edge. They love their land, they love their town. Anybody who says anything bad about any of it is not going to be taken well."

article.story: Memphis (7-2) at South Florida (6-3), Nov. 12 at 8 p.m. EST. Opening Line: Memphis by 6.5. Against the spread: Memphis 5-4, South Florida 4-5. How to watch: ESPN Key stats Memphis Offense Overall: 514.0 yards per game (5th in FBS) Passing: 290.6 yards per game (13th) Rushing: 223.4 yards per game (9th) Scoring: 37.6 points per game (14th) Memphis Defense Overall: 376.3 yards per game (81st in FBS) Passing: 189.1 yards per game (33rd) Rushing: 187.2 yards per game (122nd) Scoring: 23.6 points per game (59th) South Florida Offense Overall: 319.1 yards per game (123rd in FBS) Passing: 170.9 yards per game (126th) Rushing: 148.2 yards per game (76th) Scoring: 25.9 points per game (88th) South Florida Defense Overall: 312.7 yards per game (25th in FBS) Passing: 183.3 yards per game (23rd) Rushing: 129.3 yards per game (49th) Scoring: 15.1 points per game (10th) South Florida is 93rd in third down percentage, converting 37.3% of the time. Memphis ranks 16th on defense, allowing its opponents at convert at 31.1%. South Florida ranks 14th in the FBS with a +7 turnover margin. Both teams avoid getting penalized. Memphis ranks 25th in the FBS averaging 44.6 penalty yards per game, and South Florida ranks 9th with a 38.9-yard average. Memphis is 82nd in FBS in red zone offense, scoring on 84.1% of trips. South Florida's red zone defense ranks 29th at 77.3%. Team leaders Memphis Passing: Marcus Stokes, 2,532 yards, 25 TDs, 6 INTs, 69.1 completion percentage Rushing: Jaylin Carter, 929 yards on 151 carries, 10 TDs Receiving: Hunter Tipton, 495 yards on 35 catches, 5 TDs South Florida Passing: Michael Van Buren Jr., 1,299 yards, 6 TDs, 0 INTs, 64.1 completion percentage Rushing: D.J. Crowther, 689 yards on 138 carries, 7 TDs Receiving: Bryson Rodgers, 395 yards on 38 catches, 3 TDs Last game Memphis defeated Army 49-22 on Oct. 31. Stokes passed for 371 yards on 29-of-35 attempts (82.9%) with four touchdowns and no interceptions. He also carried the ball seven times for 30 yards. Carter had 96 rushing yards on 23 carries and two touchdowns, adding four receptions for 22 yards. Jermane Hayes put up 86 yards on nine catches with two touchdowns. South Florida lost 20-17 to East Carolina on Nov. 6. Luke Kromenhoek threw for 179 yards on 17-of-21 attempts (81.0%) with one touchdown and no interceptions. Crowther carried the ball 17 times for 111 yards, adding three receptions for 42 yards. Rodgers had five receptions for 50 yards and one touchdown. Next game Memphis plays at Navy on Nov. 21. South Florida plays at Florida Atlantic on Nov. 21.
